Theta.summary: The kernel `θ(r, t)` in Yor's formula (1.1): `r/√(2π³t) · e^{π²/(2t)} ∫₀^∞ e^{−u²/(2t)} e^{−r cosh u} sinh u sin(πu/t) du`.
Theta.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

TimeReversal.summary: Brownian time reversal on a fixed interval: `timeReversed` maps `W` to `s ↦ W_t − W_{t−s}`, and the module proves that this process is again a Brownian motion on `[0, t]` by computing its covariance and checking it is Gaussian. This is the ingredient behind the paper's identity (1.3).
TimeReversal.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

TruncLog.summary: A truncated logarithm `truncLog n`, clipped to `[−n, n]` on `(0, ∞)` and `0` elsewhere: a bounded measurable approximation of `log` that converges to it pointwise as `n → ∞`.
TruncLog.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

TwinGenerator.summary: The generator of `(expIntTwin, B)` applied to a product test function: the integrand of (3.4b). Includes its joint continuity.
TwinGenerator.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

UpperGamma.summary: The upper incomplete Gamma function `Γ(s, x)`, used in the closed form of the Asian inner integral (p. 1091).
UpperGamma.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

WaldIncrementFromPaths.summary: The Wald (exponential-martingale) increment written as a functional of continuous paths, with its continuity in time and measurability.
WaldIncrementFromPaths.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YCrit.summary: The critical point `y₀(v) = ½ log(1 + 2v)` of `y ↦ A(v, y)`.
YCrit.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YMinus.summary: The lower inverse branch `y_−(v, a) = log(a − √(a² − (1 + 2v)))` of the characteristic `A(v, ·)`, with smoothness and the fact that it inverts `A` below `y₀(v)`.
YMinus.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YPlus.summary: The upper inverse branch `y_+(v, a) = log(a + √(a² − (1 + 2v)))` of the characteristic `A(v, ·)`, with smoothness and the fact that it inverts `A` above `y₀(v)`.
YPlus.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorAnalytic.summary: Regularity of Yor's conditional density for `σ = 2`. It is `C^∞` on `(0, ∞) × ℝ`, every mixed partial derivative is an explicit finite sum of basis terms, and boundary limits at `0⁺` and `∞` plus Gaussian-weighted moment bounds hold. Together these prove Proposition 2.2 constructively (`prop_2_2_constructive`).
YorAnalytic.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorClassical.summary: Yor's joint density formula (1.1), stated as `yor_joint_density_classical` and proved by the constructive route in `YorJointDensity`. The name is kept as the citation point for Yor's theorem.
YorClassical.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorDensity.summary: Yor's candidate joint density for `σ = 2` from (1.1), built from `θ`: `(1/x) e^{−(1+e^{2y})/(2x)} θ(e^y/x, t)` on `x > 0`, and `0` otherwise.
YorDensity.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorJointDensity.summary: Proof that Yor's formula (1.1) really is the joint density of `(∫₀ᵗ e^{2W_s} ds, W_t)`. It evaluates the exact `1/x`-Laplace transform of `yorDensity`, gives uniform integrability bounds, proves continuity and nonnegativity, and matches the joint law against test functions.
YorJointDensity.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorKernel.summary: Analysis of the Hartman–Watson integral kernel behind `θ`: the formal derivatives `Jm t m`, their continuity and smoothness on `(0, ∞)`, the derivative recursion `J_m' = J_{m+1}`, vanishing at `r = 0`, and exponential decay at infinity and polynomial decay at `0⁺`.
YorKernel.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

YorLaplace.summary: The Hartman–Watson/Yor contour identity, proved with a Cauchy rectangle contour: the `1/x`-Laplace transform of Yor's density has the closed form used to identify the joint law.
YorLaplace.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

ZpowPath.summary: A path functional giving a reciprocal power of the finite-horizon `Z`, built from a continuous path with fixed initial capital, together with its measurability.
ZpowPath.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source

Zproc.summary: The process `Z_t` of (3.1), built from two independent Brownian motions as `e^{σ(νt − B_t)}(∫₀^∞ e^{σ(νs+W_s)} ds + ∫₀ᵗ e^{σ(−νs+B_s)} ds)`.
Zproc.author: Grok Bot (AI), 2026-11-18, from the Lean source
